clue.text: Western dollars corrupted Dacre's "Enemies of the People"

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreign money has bribed a newspaper editor into running an inflammatory front page.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Dacre edited the Daily Mail, which in 2016 ran the headline 'Enemies of the People' over photos of three senior judges who ruled on Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: The judges attacked in that headline sat in the senior judiciary, the peers once known by this title in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Where Hollywood's rising star Johnny drank

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, abbreviated LA

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the surname runs backwards

parts.note: Johnny Depp is a Hollywood star

explanation.surface: A film star's drinking spot is pointed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat drinks milk by scooping it with its tongue, so this verb means drank.

clue.text: Russia supports Trump's unfinished construction project; that'll show Tusk!

indicators.note: in a down clue supports means sitting underneath, so the country goes below
unfinished means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Trump's planned border wall is the building project
RUS is the international code for Russia

explanation.surface: Russia backs Trump's half-built wall, which will teach the European Council's Donald Tusk a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Tusk was President of the European Council; here 'Tusk' is just a tusk.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arctic animal displays a pair of long ivory tusks, so it is something that shows a tusk.

clue.text: Spontaneously translated "em, upsilon"

indicators.note: translated means converted into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone renders two Greek letter names on the spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'em' and 'upsilon' look like the names of letters, but they are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without forethought, on a sudden urge, is doing something spontaneously.

clue.text: English no 1 seed desperate to put up a strong defence

definitions.text: to put up a strong defence

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the numeral 1 resembles the letter I

explanation.surface: England's top-seeded tennis player is fighting hard to stay in the tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to resist stubbornly and refuse to give ground, a determined defence.

clue.text: Remove gun from Detective Inspector (Special Branch)

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector
an arm is a branch, as of a river or an organisation

explanation.surface: A police officer from Special Branch is being relieved of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special Branch' reads as the British police unit, but it splits into two pieces, S and ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a weapon away from someone is the plain meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Plaid a "hopeless case" for part of the Northwest

indicators.note: the case holds the letters, which sit inside the words plaid a hopeless

explanation.surface: Plaid Cymru, the Welsh nationalist party, is called hopeless in north-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state lies in the Pacific Northwest region of America.

clue.text: The local birds stripped David Stubbs; nothing whatsoever covered!

indicators.note: in a down clue covered means one piece sits on top of the next
stripped means the outer letters of the name David are removed

parts.note: FA, short for sweet Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing at all
Una Stubbs is a British actress

explanation.surface: A man called David Stubbs is undressed with nothing covering him.
explanation.walkthrough: Una Stubbs is the actress, not David: the first name is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird life of a particular region is its population of birds, the term ornithologists use.

clue.text: Knut's chaps engage individual bankers

indicators.note: engage means take on or hold, so the setter's chaps hold the other piece

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so his chaps are 'my men'
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: The setter's team take on a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Financiers who handle large sums are informally called by this term.

clue.text: One possible scenario: "it's a poor participation rate" Theresa admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the prime minister's surname goes inside
poor here means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: turnout is the share of voters who take part
Theresa May was then the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Theresa May concedes that voter participation may be low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like a comment on the turnout, but it is the anagram signal for 'it's a'; 'admitted' puts the Prime Minister's surname in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a hypothetical outcome, how events might happen to unfold.

clue.text: Revolting, sickly, nasty smell about TV channel in the home of democracy?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the smell word goes round the other piece

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: revolting is read as turning over, so the word for sickly runs backwards

parts.note: sickly means ill
a station is a broadcasting channel

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a disgusting stink around a television company's premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like a description of the smell, but it is the reversal signal for the word meaning sickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters cast their ballots at this venue, so it is playfully where democracy lives; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: See 10
Supply election's first gag

indicators.note: the first letter of the word election is taken

parts.note: a gag is a joke, a quip

explanation.surface: A campaign's opening joke is offered up.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what they need is to provide or kit them out, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Relatively few around November said "that's a lie, Prime Minister"

parts.note: 'not so' is a flat denial that something is true

indicators.note: around puts the prime minister's name on either side of the letter for November

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone in November accuses the Prime Minister of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY is split open by N to make MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a fairly small number, a modest quantity compared with what might be expected.

clue.text: Karr saw Baron Cohen taking Charlie in dive

indicators.note: in places the comedian-with-Charlie piece inside the word for dive

parts.note: a plunge is a dive

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the comedian's first name takes in the extra letter

parts.note: Sacha Baron Cohen is the comedian behind Borat
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone watched a comedian dive into the water with a friend called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is not the past of see but a noun, a saying. Alphonse Karr wrote 'plus ça change, plus c'est la même chose'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, and this French phrase is the maxim coined by the writer Karr.

clue.text: Wall of Jericho over damp-course

indicators.note: the run of letters flows like a course through the words Jericho over damp

explanation.surface: The walls of Jericho have a layer laid above a damp-proof course.
explanation.walkthrough: A damp-course is a waterproof layer in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: This huge concrete barrier on the Colorado River is a dam, a wall that holds back water.

clue.text: Having calmed down, name-dropper Julian welcomes United director

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the shortened surname holds the extra letter
a name-dropper here drops N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Julian Assange is the WikiLeaks founder
U is short for United in team names

explanation.surface: Julian Assange, a known name-dropper, cools off after letting in a football club's director.
explanation.definitionFit: To be soothed or pacified is to have one's anger or pain eased, a calming.

clue.text: Gay community synonymous with race relations?

parts.note: camp is used to mean flamboyantly gay
a town is a community

explanation.surface: A gay neighbourhood is held up as a model of harmony between ethnic groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race relations' suggests ethnicity; the race is the horse race in the song 'Camptown Races'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Foster's minstrel song made this place name inseparable from its races.

clue.text: Political gambit gets Latinos furious with Pence

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Hispanic voters are enraged by the American Vice President.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a vote at short notice to exploit a lead in the polls is a calculated political move.

clue.text: Ives holding first-class return for last service

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the singer's first name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Burl Ives was an American folk singer

indicators.note: return means turning back, so the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class

explanation.surface: Someone named Ives holds a first-class return ticket for the final train.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral is the final rite held for someone, the interment of the body.

clue.text: Gave story to the media, though not watertight

definitions.meaning: passed confidential information to the press
letting water seep out through a hole

explanation.surface: A source briefed the press even though the story had holes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both disclosing secrets unofficially and escaping through a crack.

clue.text: A bit like Corbyn, Ron Paul up for revolution

indicators.note: revolution means turning things over, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A US libertarian is ready for an uprising, rather like the British Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn, Labour leader at the time, polled poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbyn then had weak approval ratings, so the clue calls him somewhat disliked by the public.

clue.text: Write cover for California classic American Pie

indicators.note: cover for means one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to pen is to write
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to write sleeve notes for a California edition of Don McLean's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Pie' looks like the song title, but it is just a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie made with this nut is a traditional dessert in the US, especially at Thanksgiving.

clue.text: Notes written to help Gertrude, stripped of German rights

indicators.note: stripped of means having things taken away, so letters leave the name

parts.note: R stands for right, so two rights are RR

explanation.surface: A woman named Gertrude loses her German citizenship rights.
explanation.walkthrough: G, R and R are removed from GERTRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A study is a piece of music written to help a player practise a technique, a set of notes for learning.

clue.text: Typical primo/starter for Cheech and Chong, going out to get Italian

indicators.note: going out suggests things spilling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
for here is read as the starting letter of the name that follows, taking just its first letter

explanation.surface: The stoner comedy duo Cheech and Chong head out for an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' belongs to the definition with 'primo', not to Cheech: the anagram is of C and CHONG.
explanation.definitionFit: These potato dumplings are a classic first course in an Italian meal, which Italians call the primo.

clue.text: One in torment over Liberal Democrat Clegg

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
LD is short for Liberal Democrat
Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A former party leader is suffering torment once again.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a nickname for the devil, the being who torments sinners in hell.

clue.text: Row in government at table

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out in the cabinet as they sit round the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seated at table means eating a meal, which is having dinner.

clue.text: Son fell, having tripped

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to tumble is to fall

explanation.surface: A boy took a tumble after catching his foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe losing footing and nearly falling, so they are close synonyms.
